articles.title: ¿Deberías volver a los auriculares con cable? Por esto Kylie Jenner y otras celebridades lo están haciendo
articles.summary: ¿Por qué tantas celebridades usan auriculares con cable? No es porque tus AirPods no se sujeten bien.
articles.body:
Si eres mayor como yo (o, en todo caso, un millennial que está envejeciendo), quizá hayas notado una extraña tendencia tecnológica últimamente: los audífonos con cable están volviendo a ponerse de moda. Desde Kylie Jenner y Hailey Bieber hasta Ariana Grande y Dua Lipa, todas han sido vistas llevando o usando un par. La semana pasada, una publicación viral en X que señalaba esta tendencia desató una ola de especulaciones entre usuarios de X y Reddit sobre la posibilidad de que las celebridades sepan algo que nosotros, los simples mortales, desconocemos: tus audífonos inalámbricos pueden ser hackeados.

Pero ¿hay algo de cierto en esa afirmación? Afortunadamente, probablemente no necesites tirar a la basura tus AirPods de US$250. Esto es lo que debes saber.

¿Pueden hackear tus audífonos inalámbricos Bluetooth?

Técnicamente, casi cualquier cosa puede ser hackeada si alguien tiene suficiente tiempo, paciencia y equipos costosos para hacerlo. Sin embargo, las probabilidades de que una persona cualquiera se tome la molestia de espiar el pódcast que escuchas durante tu trayecto matutino al trabajo son bastante bajas.

Bluetooth, el protocolo inalámbrico que utiliza tu teléfono para conectarse a los audífonos inalámbricos, tiene sus vulnerabilidades como cualquier otra tecnología, pero emplea diversas técnicas de seguridad , como el cifrado, para dificultar que los hackers las aprovechen. Puedes evitar la mayoría de los problemas asegurándote de desvincular tu teléfono de los dispositivos antiguos que ya no utilizas y manteniéndolo siempre actualizado. Si quieres extremar las precauciones, puedes desactivar el Bluetooth de tu teléfono o computadora portátil cuando no lo estés utilizando.

La realidad es que la mayoría de nosotros no somos objetivos de alguien que quiera utilizar Bluetooth como vía de acceso para un ataque informático. Es mucho más probable que seas víctima de una estafa de phishing o de un ataque de ransomware .

En cambio, los políticos, los ejecutivos empresariales y otras personas que podrían ser objetivos de espionaje tienen más probabilidades de sufrir un ataque a través de Bluetooth. Un caso conocido es el de la exvicepresidenta Kamala Harris, quien le contó a Stephen Colbert que utiliza audífonos con cable debido a la información a la que tuvo acceso durante reuniones informativas clasificadas cuando formaba parte del Senado. "No vayas en el tren usando tus audífonos y pensando que nadie puede escuchar tu conversación", dijo Harris.

Entonces, ¿por qué vemos audífonos con cable por todas partes?

En el caso de las celebridades que utilizan audífonos con cable, efectivamente se trata de una tendencia. La nostalgia por los años 2000 está muy de moda en estos momentos , ¿y qué hay más representativo de esa época que los audífonos con cable? Harper's Bazaar los ha declarado el "accesorio más cool de las chicas de moda" . Además, combinan muy bien con dispositivos tecnológicos retro como los iPod, que también están regresando , al igual que antes lo hicieron los casetes y los discos de vinilo.

También hay algunas razones prácticas. Los audífonos con cable no necesitan cargarse, así que nunca te quedarás sin batería a mitad de una canción. Y, como señaló Mike Muse, colaborador de ABC News, en un segmento de septiembre , los cables transmiten la idea de que quien los lleva es más "cool" y tiene "los pies en la tierra" en un mundo cada vez más digital. Dado el ritmo de los cambios y la ansiedad que genera la inteligencia artificial , no resulta tan sorprendente que algunas personas estén optando por una apariencia más analógica en sus dispositivos tecnológicos personales.

Así que no sientas que tienes que deshacerte de tus audífonos inalámbricos por miedo a algún problema de seguridad oculto. Pero si quieres seguir las últimas tendencias, los audífonos con cable definitivamente están viviendo su momento.

articles.title: Identifican fósil que estuvo guardado durante 100 años como un nuevo pariente del 'T-rex'
articles.summary: Estos dinosaurios habrían sido más peligrosos para los humanos que un tiranosaurio rex, afirman los científicos
articles.body:
Un fósil que había pasado desapercibido durante mucho tiempo y que se conservaba en un museo ha sido identificado como un nuevo pariente del T-rex , el primero de su grupo descubierto en Europa .

Para identificar a la especie de dinosaurio carnívoro de largas garras, del tamaño aproximado de un tigre grande, se utilizó un fósil de cráneo encontrado en la isla de Wight, Reino Unido , en 1924.

Pertenece a un grupo de carnívoros ágiles de dos patas llamados Megaraptora , estrechamente relacionados con los tiranosaurios, incluido el poderoso Tyrannosaurus rex .

Este grupo ha sido el más misterioso de los grandes dinosaurios carnívoros, ya que hasta la fecha se han encontrado pocos fósiles de megaraptor.

"Es un verdadero misterio que este fósil pasara desapercibido durante tanto tiempo, guardado en un cajón durante casi 100 años. En la isla de Wight se encuentran muchos huesos; quién sabe qué más habrá por descubrir", declaró el paleontólogo Cassius Morrison, del University College de Londres . El fósil se conservaba en el Museo de Historia Natural de la capital británica.

La nueva especie, denominada Invictibellatrix amberina, tenía la cabeza delgada y atacaba a sus presas con sus grandes brazos y garras curvas gigantes en lugar de sus mandíbulas.

El vocablo Invictibellatrix , que indica el género biológico del dinosaurio, significa "guerrera invicta" y los investigadores argumentan que el nombre fue elegido con la intención de "dar esperanza y fuerza a todas aquellas que son acosadas, discriminadas, victimizadas y oprimidas, para que sepan que el mañana será suyo y que no se rindan ante tales adversidades".

El nombre específico de la especie, amberina , hace referencia al ámbar que se encuentra en las rocas donde se descubrió el fósil.

"Según lo que sabemos de sus parientes más cercanos, Invictibellatrix habría medido entre 3 y 4 m de largo y poco más de 1,5 m de altura, aproximadamente la misma altura que un ser humano", indicó Morrison.

Explicó que probablemente habría tenido plumas y sus garras podrían haber medido entre 10 y 20 cm de largo. Se habría alimentado de pequeños dinosaurios, lagartos y mamíferos, que en la cadena alimentaria actual equivaldría a la hiena", explicó.

Aunque no fue el depredador alfa de su época, I. amberina habría sido más peligroso para los humanos que un T-rex , dicen los investigadores.

"Habríamos sido presas del tamaño perfecto, aproximadamente un tercio de su peso corporal. Sin duda nos habrían perseguido. Un T-rex no se habría molestado, ya que seríamos demasiado pequeños", afirmó Morrison.

Se cree que los megaraptores se originaron en Asia , antes de migrar a través de Europa y convertirse en los depredadores dominantes en toda la masa continental meridional de Gondwana, que incluye la actual África , Sudamérica y la Antártida .

"Esta nueva especie es la primera prueba que tenemos de que los megaraptores también estuvieron presentes en Europa y que llegaron a Gondwana de esta manera, en lugar de desplazarse de isla en isla más al sur", planteó Charlie Scherer, otro de los autores del estudio publicado en la revista Royal Society Open Science.

En el estudio, los científicos realizaron tomografías computarizadas de la parte posterior del cráneo fósil, creando así un modelo 3D del mismo, así como un modelo del interior del cráneo.

Luego compararon el modelo con los cráneos de tiranosaurios, espinosaurios, raptores y otros dinosaurios carnívoros bípedos.

Los investigadores hallaron en el fósil una combinación única de características craneales, incluyendo un orificio ovalado por donde la médula espinal entraba al cerebro y una cresta en forma de reloj de arena, lo que ayudó a concluir que, efectivamente, pertenecía a una especie aún no descubierta.

Un análisis más detallado del cráneo reveló que el dinosaurio pertenecía a la familia de los megaraptores.

Los hallazgos ayudan a comprender mejor la propagación de los megaraptores por todo el mundo a lo largo del tiempo. Según concluyeron los científicos, estos dinosaurios estaban ampliamente distribuidos a nivel mundial durante el Cretácico Inferior, en la época de Invictibellatrix.

Pero a finales del Cretácico, decenas de millones de años después, probablemente se habían extinguido en la gigantesca masa continental septentrional de Laurasia, que incluye la Europa actual.

Durante este último periodo, los megaraptores se convirtieron en los depredadores dominantes en todo el sur de Gondwana, alcanzando tamaños gigantescos, con garras de hasta 35 cm de largo, según afirman los científicos.

Asimismo, creen probable que los megaraptores se extinguieran en el norte debido a cambios en el clima o el medio ambiente, o a la presencia de depredadores competidores como otros tiranosaurios.

"A pesar de más de 200 años de recolección de fósiles, la isla de Wight continúa sorprendiéndonos con nuevas especies de dinosaurios, y los hallazgos de dinosaurios carnívoros, como Invictibellatrix, han sido particularmente inusuales", observó el autor principal del estudio, Paul Barrett.

"Trabajos como este demuestran el valor excepcional de investigar colecciones de museos históricos, donde aún quedan muchos descubrimientos por hacer", comentó Barrett.

articles.title: La nube más extraña de Marte de hasta 1,800 kilómetros juega con unas leyes físicas que nadie había visto antes
articles.summary: Cada mañana, junto a un volcán gigante de Marte, una estela blanca se estira sobre el paisaje y se esfuma antes de que acabe el día. Los científicos creían c...
articles.body:
En Marte hay una nube que parece seguir un régimen estricto. Durante varios meses de la primavera y el verano del hemisferio sur del planeta rojo, una estela blanca de hielo de agua aparece cada mañana junto al volcán Arsia Mons, se alarga sobre el paisaje y se esfuma antes de que acabe el día. Al amanecer siguiente, la escena se repite. Pero lo más extraño no es su tamaño, sino el proceso al que han tenido que recurrir los científicos para explicar su origen, hasta ahora considerado poco probable en la práctica.

Se llama nube alargada de Arsia Mons (AMEC) y, según la Agencia Espacial Europea (ESA), puede extenderse hasta 1.800 kilómetros, casi la distancia que separa Bogotá de Lima en línea recta. Se forma junto a Arsia Mons –en el lado opuesto por el que llega el viento– y fue la sonda Mars Express, de la propia ESA, la que la identificó en 2018 y ha seguido sus apariciones desde entonces.

Las imágenes revelaron que se trata de una nube orográfica, como las que surgen en la Tierra cuando el viento atraviesa zonas montañosas. No obstante, los modelos meteorológicos convencionales no conseguían reproducir su forma y evolución.

La pista que faltaba para ello la encontró el equipo de Jorge Hernández-Bernal, del LMD/CNRS/Sorbonne Université, al introducir en las simulaciones un mecanismo que hasta entonces solo se había considerado teóricamente para las atmósferas planetarias y que nunca se había observado directamente en ellas.

"Una vez que incorporamos estos fenómenos físicos a nuestras simulaciones, el AMEC surgió tal y como esperábamos", explicó Hernández-Bernal en un comunicado de la ESA.

Nucleación homogénea: de la teoría a Marte

La clave estaba en cómo se llega a formar el hielo. En condiciones normales, las partículas que flotan en la atmósfera sirven de punto de apoyo para que el vapor de agua, al enfriarse, forme gotas o cristales de hielo. En Marte, ese papel se atribuye principalmente al polvo. Pero la AMEC parece saltarse ese paso: el hielo se formaría directamente a partir del vapor, sin necesitar ninguna partícula a la que adherirse.

"Es como si las gotitas de condensación aparecieran en medio de una habitación, en lugar de en una ventana", dijo Hernández-Bernal.

Ese proceso se llama nucleación homogénea y, según el investigador, nunca se había visto en la atmósfera de un planeta. Era, resume, "totalmente inesperado".

El estudio, publicado en Nature Geoscience, señala que ya se había planteado como posibilidad para las nubes mesosféricas de la Tierra y Venus, pero nunca se había observado en la naturaleza. La dificultad está en las condiciones excepcionales que necesita. Según la ESA, este mecanismo exigiría niveles extremos de sobresaturación, con una humedad relativa más de 100.000 veces superior a la que experimentamos habitualmente en la Tierra.

Ahí entra en juego el volcán. Su enorme tamaño cambia el movimiento de los vientos a su alrededor y provoca una onda atmosférica. El resultado es un ascenso vertiginoso del aire húmedo, que gana varios kilómetros de altura en cuestión de minutos. La temperatura cae 30 grados en solo 10 minutos. En esas condiciones, según el modelo, el vapor de agua formaría directamente cristales de hielo, dando origen a la nube.

Según los investigadores, la delgada atmósfera marciana y la altura del volcán se combinan para crear las condiciones excepcionales que favorecerían este proceso.

A pesar de los resultados observados, el modelo no es perfecto. Y es que la simulación todavía presenta diferencias respecto a lo que muestran las observaciones de Mars Express. Aun así, Hernández-Bernal considera "notable" el resultado, especialmente porque los científicos disponen de mucha menos información sobre la atmósfera marciana que sobre la terrestre.

Para desarrollar la simulación, el equipo utilizó datos de tres instrumentos de Mars Express: la Cámara de Monitorización Visual, la Cámara Estereoscópica de Alta Resolución y OMEGA. La sonda cuenta, además, con una ventaja importante al ser una de las pocas naves en órbita alrededor de Marte, junto con ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter, capaz de realizar observaciones por la mañana, cuando aparece la nube.

El descubrimiento podría tener consecuencias más allá de Marte. Según los autores del estudio, los resultados invitan a revisar algunas hipótesis sobre la formación de nubes en la Tierra y, potencialmente, en otros planetas. Como señala Colin Wilson, científico del proyecto Mars Express de la ESA, comprender esta nube ha requerido una física exótica, "y esto podría ser cierto en otros lugares del cosmos".

articles.title: Child among 2 killed after vehicle drives onto soccer field at Kansas sports complex
articles.summary: A child and an adult were killed after a vehicle drove onto a soccer field at a Wichita sports complex. Police said the driver was taken into custody
articles.body: Two people, including a child, were killed, and several others injured Saturday when a vehicle drove onto a soccer field at a sports complex in Wichita, Kansas. The driver, identified as a 34-year-old woman, was taken into custody following the incident at Stryker Sports Complex, Wichita Police Capt. Aaron Moses said in a news conference. Police said they believe the woman had a child playing soccer at the complex that day, but not on the field where the deadly crash took place. Sedgwick County emergency dispatchers began receiving multiple calls about the incident around 3:25 p.m., Moses said. FORMER TV ANCHOR WHO PLEADED GUILTY TO KILLING MOTHER LAST HALLOWEEN GETS LIFE SENTENCE Police and emergency crews responded to the complex, where two people were pronounced dead on the field and 11 others, including five children, were transported to area hospitals. Police confirmed that a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were pronounced dead at the scene. Both were from McPherson, Kansas, but authorities said they were not related. Moses said ten victims suffered traumatic injuries ranging from minor bruises to extremely serious injuries. Those injuries were believed to be non-life-threatening, he added. The injured children included two 5-year-olds, two 8-year-olds and a 9-year-old girl, according to Moses. A 61-year-old woman was also transported for a nontraumatic medical issue. Two juveniles were inside the vehicle at the time of the incident, Moses said. The vehicle remained at the scene, and police said the driver posed no additional ongoing threat to the public. "This is a tragedy," Moses said. The Kansas State High School Activities Association (KSHSAA) suspended play at its inaugural girls flag football state championship following the incident, which occurred on an adjacent field at Stryker Sports Complex. LOYAL DOG FETCHES POLICE TO HELP OWNER WHO FELL AT KANSAS HOME The association said games would not resume this weekend and that updated game times would be announced later. Authorities have not confirmed whether the driver acted intentionally, or whether a medical emergency, impairment or another factor caused the deadly crash. Moses said the driver had a valid driver's license and no outstanding arrest warrants. He said the driver was cooperating with the investigation. No charges have been announced. Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan emphasized that investigators know what happened but have not yet established why. "We know what happened, but now we're working very hard to find out why it happened," Sullivan said. TEXAS WOMAN SENTENCED TO 7 YEARS IN PRISON, ANNUAL JAIL TIME DURING PROBATION FOR DEADLY DUI CRASH Sullivan also praised community members who rushed to help those injured at the complex before first responders arrived. "It was truly amazing." Wichita Mayor Lily Wu called the incident "heartbreaking." "No one could have imagined the tragedy that would unfold," she said. The Sedgwick County Sheriff's Office, Bel Aire Police Department, Kansas Highway Patrol, Wichita Fire Department and Sedgwick County Emergency Medical Services were among the agencies responding to the scene. Investigators said they have interviewed more than 30 witnesses at the scene and were reviewing evidence, including video and photographs. Officials asked anyone with video footage of the incident to submit it to authorities.

articles.title: Conor Kennedy, RFK Jr's son, celebrates wedding with Brazilian pop star in gorgeous setting
articles.summary: In Rio de Janeiro, Conor Kennedy and Giulia Be celebrated their wedding across three days, including a blessing at Christ the Redeemer and a ceremony at a historic 1808 church.
articles.body: Rio de Janeiro’s beaches, mountaintops and historic streets were among the scenes of the wedding celebration of Conor Kennedy and Brazilian pop star Giulia Bourguignon Marinho earlier this month — with plenty of images circulating across social media in recent days. Conor Kennedy is a son of Robert F. Kennedy Jr., secretary of Health & Human Services in the Trump administration. The three-day wedding celebration, which kicked off Oct. 8, included a blessing at the iconic Christ the Redeemer statue, a ceremony at the downtown church Igreja Nossa Senhora do Carmo da Antiga Sé and a reception at a historic mansion in Jardim Botânico, according to reports. The couple officially married in a private civil ceremony in Los Angeles in March, Vogue reported. FANS SWARM JFK JR. SITES IN MAJOR CITY AS HIT SERIES ‘LOVE STORY’ TRIGGERS TOURISM FRENZY "We wanted to celebrate not just the wedding, but also Rio de Janeiro, the city we love," Marinho, who is professionally known as Giulia Be, told the outlet. "Being there, overlooking Rio, with our family was one of those moments I’ll never forget." Earlier this year, Marinho told Brazilian outlet Globo she saw it as "the only chance to bring all of [Kennedy's] friends and all of his family to Brazil," and she "wanted to show them a good time." She recalled that she told her then-fiancé, "'My love, I love you, but I’m not getting married in Massachusetts.'" CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES The church where the couple's ceremony was held, commonly called the Antiga Sé, sits in Rio’s historic center. It dates back to 1808, when, after the Portuguese royal court arrived in Brazil, it served as their royal chapel and cathedral. Nearby Praça XV de Novembro is a historic square that hosts a Saturday flea market, where shoppers browse antiques, records and clothes, according to The New York Times. The area also offers visitors proximity to other historic sites and waterfront views. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The festivities reportedly began with a welcome party in the hills of Alto da Boa Vista. The next day, guests joined the couple for beach volleyball on Ipanema before attending the blessing at Christ the Redeemer, atop Corcovado Mountain. The statue sits within Tijuca National Park, where visitors can take in views across the city. The reception took place at Instituto Brando Barbosa in the neighborhood of Jardim Botânico, which is home to the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden, a public attraction known for its plant collection and historic grounds. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Conor Kennedy is a grandson of the late Sen. Robert F. Kennedy, President John F. Kennedy's brother. Vogue noted that Marinho's Calvin Klein slip dress for the wedding blessing evoked the understated elegance of Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, Conor Kennedy’s late aunt by marriage. RFK Jr. shared family photos from the festivities on social media. Pictures showed the wedding party beneath the Christ the Redeemer statue; his wife, Cheryl Hines, pictured alongside samba dancers; and the newly married couple checking their phones for updates on the Seminoles-Cardinals game. In a response on Instagram, his new daughter-in-law commented, "Love you, Bobby." articles.title: The Diane Watson playground murder: Trauma, loss and a love that endured
articles.summary: Diane Watson's best friend Pauline recalls a shocking school murder and its lasting legacy.
articles.body:
When Diane Watson was stabbed to death in the playground of a Glasgow school in 1991, her best friend Pauline was standing by her side.

Pauline watched as 16-year-old Diane collapsed after the knife attack by another pupil and then helped to carry her across the road to the arms of her parents who lived in an upstairs flat within view of the school.

Diane's murder would not only devastate her family, her friends and the local community, its shockwaves would go on to be felt for decades.

Warning - this story contains descriptions of violence, death and suicide.

Thirty-five years later, Pauline Love Thomson has spoken for the first time about the trauma of that April morning when she was just 16.

In a new BBC Scotland podcast, Crime Next Door: The Playground Murder , she relives the day 15-year-old Barbara Glover came to Whitehill secondary school in Glasgow's east end armed with a large kitchen knife.

Pauline describes how a large crowd of schoolkids gathered round as Glover shouted at Diane while waving the knife - and the chilling moment she dealt the deadly blow.

"She actually let out a growl when she stepped forward," Pauline says.

"She stabbed her and people started just moving away. Everybody just vanished.

"I went over, I just put my arm around her [Diane's] shoulder because I hadn't actually appreciated the damage that the knife would have done. It was a big knife."

Pauline tried to help her bleeding friend get home to the flat across the road she shared with her mum, dad and brother Alan.

She recalls Diane saying: "I don't believe it. She stabbed me."

It was only a short distance to the flat but Pauline felt her friend slumping even before they reached the school gate.

With the help of two other girls she got Diane across the road but by the time she reached the entrance to the flat, she collapsed.

Her father Jim, who had been alerted by another girl battering on his door, ran down and took his daughter in his arms.

He carried her upstairs and desperately tried to revive her as her mother Margaret and 15-year-old brother looked on in horror.

Jim tried to give her mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, Pauline said.

"I'm shouting, 'you're not doing it right'," she said.

"I could hear her gurgling. There was blood coming out her mouth."

Diane Watson was later declared dead at Glasgow Royal Infirmary and Barbara Glover handed herself into the police.

Three months later, Pauline was the first to give evidence at Glover's trial.

She told the court that in the days leading up to the stabbing Glover had been hassling Diane.

It was only later, she said, that she found out it was because Glover thought Diane had been going out with her ex-boyfriend.

This had culminated in a fight outside a shop which ended with Glover's hoodie being pulled up and her bra exposed, making her feel humiliated.

The following morning the schoolgirl put a kitchen knife in her bag and took the bus to school where she stabbed Diane to death.

Pauline said Diane was not interested in the boy and that they barely knew Glover, who was in the year below them at school.

However, when Glover took the stand she told the court she had been bullied by Diane for over a year.

Pauline and others gave evidence saying Diane had never treated Glover badly.

The jury unanimously passed a guilty verdict on Glover and because she was under 16 she was detained without limit of time, meaning there was no fixed date for her release.

It was a controversial sentence which led to two journalists – Jack McLean in The Herald and Meg Henderson in Marie Claire – writing campaigning pieces about the unfairness of children being detained never knowing when they would see freedom.

Neither had attended the trial, but they both latched on to Glover's testimony that Diane was a bully.

McLean went further, introducing a class element to his claims.

He wrote that Diane "came from a background which was rather upper working class" and that she had the "smart white socks of the daughter of the Labour aristocracy".

Pauline said nothing could be further from the truth.

Margaret Watson was a dinner lady and her husband Jim was doing casual shifts as a postman.

The articles compounded the Watson family's pain at their loss and they felt Diane was being victim-blamed and besmirched.

Margaret wanted to sue but was advised they had no legal redress as it was not possible to defame the dead.

Alan, who was incredibly close to his sister, struggled deeply with her death and how she was portrayed in the media.

Less than two years after Diane was killed, he took his own life.

Pauline said newspaper and magazine cuttings about Diane were found in his hand, alongside a note saying he was sorry but he just wanted to be with his sister.

The catastrophe inside the Watsons' home sparked a decades' long crusade from Margaret.

In the chasm left by her children's deaths, she set out to challenge the power of the media and hold them to account.

She said she was not able to rest because of the malicious lies printed about her daughter and demanded an apology from The Herald and Marie Claire.

The former dinner lady's campaign brought her into contact with prime ministers, lords, and Hollywood actor Hugh Grant's Hacked Off campaign.

It also led to her giving powerful testimony at the Leveson Inquiry into press ethics in November 2011.

She told the judge: "Just because a person's died, their reputation shouldn't die with them.

"It shouldn't be besmirched at the will of some sick journalist."

Pauline says Margaret was small, frail and grieving but she was an "absolute spitfire".

"She was a powerhouse but she was driven by grief and anger and rage pretty much the entire time," she said.

Jim Watson died in 2020, aged 69, and Margaret a year later, at 71.

Before their deaths, both The Herald and Marie Claire apologised.

Barbara Glover was released in 2000 after serving eight and a half years.

Pauline said she agreed to speak now not only for Diane, but for Alan and their parents.

As we spoke, beside her on the sofa was her husband, Andy Thomson.

It took me a moment to take it in when they told me that Andy had been Alan's best friend.

That through all the tragedy and trauma, this couple found solace in each other and they've been married for 34 years.

Their little grandson is the light of their lives.

"We were kids and I got what she was going through because I was so close to Alan," says Andy.

"And then obviously when Alan passed away, it just drew the two of us even closer.

"And we're 34 years together, we're still going strong and always have been. And always will be."

"No one gives you a book on how to cope with trauma when you're a teenager," Pauline says.

"We were left to cope, and we helped each other. Our life hasn't been all trauma – not at all. But it has been a part of it.

"The most important thing for us was we wanted to talk about Diane and Alan, not just the names in the newspapers.

"For people to have a better understanding of them as kids – because that's what they were, they were kids. Just normal teenagers who should still be here."

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line website .

articles.title: US ambassador urges Israel to prosecute attackers of American journalist
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Rubio separately urges Israel to ‘crack down’ on settler violence after attack on photographer.
articles.body:
United States Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has demanded Israel prosecute and jail those responsible for the attack on American journalist Heidi Levine in the occupied West Bank, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said Washington wants Israel to do more to deter settler attacks.

“Attacking a female photographer is a despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards,” Huckabee wrote on X on Saturday.

“Those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend YRS in prison,” he added. “We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this.”

Rubio said on Saturday that the US State Department had inquired about the attack on Levine and that he expected to hear back from the US embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday.

“We’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing,” he told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. “We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff.”

⁠Rubio’s comments to reporters came after the widespread dissemination of video showing settlers attacking Levine, a photojournalist with The Washington Post.

Rubio said the administration of US President Donald Trump would communicate its expectations to the Israelis “to prevent that from happening in the future”.

“We don’t need that right now; Israel doesn’t need that right now,” he added.

Levine was covering Palestinians’ annual olive harvest on Friday in the occupied West Bank when Israeli settlers brutally attacked her and several Palestinians.

Israeli settlers stormed the area, beat her and stole her passport, telephone, wallet and equipment, according to witnesses.

The perpetrators, armed with bottles and slingshots, “were kicking me for like 10 minutes, and I was trying to hold onto my cameras and my bag”, Levine said.

Jasper Nathaniel, an independent journalist who witnessed the attack, told Al Jazeera that Levine “was in very, very bad shape. She couldn’t really get up off the ground.”

Levine, 64, was taken to hospital after the assault in Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah.

The American photojournalist underwent surgery on her finger, which was nearly detached from her hand, and was left with a broken rib and multiple broken vertebrae, as well as lacerations, her daughter told The Associated Press news agency.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who wants to shore up his pro-settlement right-wing base ahead of closely fought October 27 elections, claimed on Friday that Palestinians or “far-left” activists may have been responsible for the attack on Levine and other Palestinians.

Meanwhile, Ambassador Huckabee, a staunch ally of Israel who has sharply criticised Israeli settler attacks against Americans, did not identify the culprits as settlers after Netanyahu tried to sow doubt as to their identity.

The Trump-appointed ambassador met Palestinian-Americans in the occupied West Bank town of Turmus Aya in September to hear locals’ testimony about their experiences with pogroms. In August, Huckabee called a days-long Israeli settler siege an “act of terror”.

The State Department criticised Friday’s attack using a cautious tone on Levine’s beating, stating condemnation of “criminal violence by any party”.

Israeli settlers have been involved in at least 170 pogroms against Palestinians since September 27, around the start of the olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli group that monitors illegal Israeli settlements.

articles.standfirst: Aos 18 anos, Kelly Cristina Almeida Souza estudou ao longo de um ano e passou de primeira. Ela contou com apoio da mãe e de professores para enfrentar a pressão religiosa da família.
articles.summary: Aos 18 anos, Kelly Cristina Almeida Souza estudou ao longo de um ano e passou de primeira. Ela contou com apoio da mãe e de professores para enfrentar a pressão religiosa da famíli
articles.body:
Estudante de escola pública e sem dinheiro para pagar um cursinho, ela organizou o próprio cronograma de estudos e recorreu a videoaulas gratuitas, provas antigas e à ajuda de professores .

Depois de uma rotina de cerca de oito horas diárias de dedicação , a aprovação veio em 2021, na primeira chamada da universidade . Agora, aos 23, se prepara para colar grau em novembro de 2026.

A rotina de preparação foi construída em meio a outras responsabilidades. Aos 16 anos, ela trabalhava no caixa de uma padaria para juntar dinheiro e comprar um computador.

Com o apoio da mãe, deixou o emprego para se dedicar ao vestibular, enquanto conciliava os estudos com as tarefas domésticas e os cuidados dos três irmãos mais novos.

Juntas, elas também precisaram enfrentar as expectativas e pressões da família extremamente religiosa, que esperava que ela se casasse em vez de priorizar os estudos .

👉 Neste ano, a 1ª fase do Vestibular 2027 da Unicamp está marcada para domingo (18). O g1 fará a cobertura completa do dia do exame, com equipes nos locais de prova, transmissão com a resolução comentada por professores e a construção de um gabarito extraoficial . Saiba mais AQUI .

À direita, Kelly ao lado da mãe, após ser aprovada em Medicina na Unicamp, em 2021. À esquerda, a estudante em ensaio fotográfico para a formatura, em 2026. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Sem condições de pagar por um cursinho, Kelly precisou descobrir quais conteúdos estudar, como distribuir as disciplinas ao longo da semana e como acompanhar a própria evolução .

A principal ferramenta foi a internet . Ela recorria a videoaulas gratuitas no YouTube e aproveitava aulas de cursinhos que disponibilizaram parte do conteúdo gratuitamente durante a pandemia.

Para estruturar a preparação, a estudante também:

Pesquisava os assuntos mais cobrados: usava essas informações para orientar a escolha dos conteúdos.

Montou um cronograma próprio: organizava as disciplinas e estabelecia a meta de avançar em cerca de três tópicos por dia.

Resolvia provas de anos anteriores: usava os exercícios para conhecer o estilo das questões e identificar os assuntos que precisavam de mais atenção.

Fazia simulados aos sábados: aproveitava o dia para treinar o ritmo exigido pelo vestibular

Reservava os domingos para descansar: mantinha um dia livre na semana.

De segunda a sexta-feira, a rotina de Kelly chegava a aproximadamente oito horas de estudo por dia. O esquema era assim:

a manhã era dedicada principalmente às revisões e à resolução de exercícios;

Ao longo da preparação, as provas antigas também ajudavam a avaliar o desempenho e direcionar os estudos. A organização era importante porque Kelly não podia se dedicar exclusivamente aos livros. Em casa, também ajudava nas tarefas domésticas e cuidava dos três irmãos mais novos.

Apesar do cronograma organizado, Kelly enfrentou momentos de ansiedade e insegurança . No início da preparação, os resultados dos simulados ficavam abaixo das notas de corte, o que provocava frustração e fazia a jovem duvidar de que conseguiria a aprovação.

“Tinha muita ansiedade envolvida no processo, incerteza, né? Eu não comecei a minha preparação atingindo as notas de corte, muito pelo contrário, eu fazia muito abaixo. Então tinha um quê de frustração também”, relatou.

Para lidar com a pressão, ela passou a praticar yoga e meditação durante a pandemia . Por volta das 9h, interrompia os estudos para fazer os exercícios, sempre no mesmo horário, e mantinha os domingos livres para descansar.

Na semana anterior à primeira fase da Unicamp, Kelly teve uma crise de ansiedade e duvidou que conseguiria passar. Para ajudá-la a recuperar a confiança, a mãe a levou para conhecer o campus da universidade pela primeira vez .

Kelly no dia em prestou o Enem. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A medicina não era um sonho definido desde a infância . A possibilidade começou a ganhar força no segundo ano do ensino médio, quando Kelly fez o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) pela primeira vez, inicialmente para testar os próprios conhecimentos e conhecer o formato da prova.

Incentivada por uma professora de língua portuguesa, ela participou do exame e tirou 920 pontos na redação . O resultado chamou a atenção da professora, que passou a incentivá-la a considerar a medicina como uma possibilidade real.

A escolha também tinha uma motivação concreta: melhorar as condições financeiras da família . A mãe, técnica de enfermagem aposentada, sustentava a casa com cerca de um salário mínimo, como conta a estudante.

“Eu entrei no curso pensando em mudar a situação financeira da minha família mesmo. Minha mãe é técnica de enfermagem, só que ela era aposentada e ganhava um salário mínimo. Nós somos em quatro crianças lá em casa, então era uma situação financeira muito difícil”.

O apoio da mãe e a decisão de deixar o emprego

Quando decidiu se dedicar ao vestibular, Kelly precisou deixar o trabalho na padaria. Foi a mãe quem tomou a iniciativa de ir até o estabelecimento para comunicar que a filha não continuaria trabalhando.

“Ela falou: ‘Não, ela não vai trabalhar aqui não, ela vai estudar pra ser médica’”, relembrou Kelly.

O apoio também foi importante diante das expectativas de parte da família. Segundo a jovem, alguns parentes, por serem muito religiosos, esperavam que as mulheres priorizassem o casamento , e não os estudos.

“Minha família realmente é muito religiosa e tinha essa expectativa sobre as mulheres, de se casarem, de não estudar. Não era uma coisa que se esperava de uma mulher. Mas minha mãe, especificamente, sempre me ajudou muito", contou.

Kelly durante sua primeira visita à Unicamp, antes de prestar o vestibular. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A Unicamp era a principal escolha de Kelly. Ela também prestou vestibulares da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) e da Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp), chegou à segunda fase de ambas, mas não concluiu essas etapas porque o resultado da Unicamp saiu primeiro .

Em 2021, aos 18 anos, foi aprovada em medicina na primeira chamada, na 371ª posição. Kelly ingressou por uma modalidade de reserva de vagas destinada a estudantes de escola pública e candidatos autodeclarados pardos .

Para conseguir permanecer na universidade, contou inicialmente com uma bolsa de mérito destinada a estudantes cotistas e, mais tarde, também recebeu auxílio estudantil. Aos 23 anos, ela se prepara para colar grau em novembro de 2026 e pretende se especializar na área de oftalmologia.

Aos estudantes que vão prestar o vestibular da Unicamp, Kelly deixa uma mensagem de incentivo:

"Mesmo que você venha de uma escola pública, mesmo que você não tenha todas as privilégios do mundo quando você está se preparando, a gente tem, hoje em dia, um monte de ação social, um monte de ação afirmativa, lembrando que é possível , ajudando você a não deixar de sonhar. Eu vejo muita gente parando de sonhar porque não vê isso e eu acho que você tem que correr sim atrás dos seus sonhos, eu sou prova viva de que é possível ", disse.

articles.standfirst: O g1 Campinas acompanha a movimentação nos locais de prova e, após o exame, transmite ao vivo a resolução comentada das questões com gabarito extraoficial.
articles.summary: O g1 Campinas acompanha a movimentação nos locais de prova e, após o exame, transmite ao vivo a resolução comentada das questões com gabarito extraoficial.
articles.body:
A Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) aplica neste domingo (18) a 1ª fase do Vestibular 2027 , com 58.431 candidatos na disputa por 2.523 vagas em 70 cursos de graduação .

O g1 Campinas acompanha a movimentação nos locais de prova e prepara uma cobertura especial, com informações ao longo do dia e resolução comentada das questões após o exame.

A partir das 15h, o portal transmite ao vivo a resolução comentada da prova com a participação de professores convidados . Durante o programa também será elaborado um gabarito extraoficial .

A 1ª fase do vestibular é aplicada neste domingo (26), e os estudantes selecionados farão a 2ª fase nos dias 29 e 30 de novembro.

O exame começa às 9h, mas a recomendação é que os candidatos cheguem às 8h (horário de Brasília), quando abrem os portões.

O exame tem duração de até cinco horas e é composto por 72 questões de múltipla escolha , cada uma com quatro alternativas e valor de um ponto.

Elas estão distribuídas entre as seguintes disciplinas:

12 de língua portuguesa e literaturas de língua portuguesa

documento de identidade original indicado no momento da inscrição;

canetas de cor preta, fabricadas em material transparente;

régua transparente e compasso são opcionais.

De acordo com as orientações divulgadas pela Comvest, os candidatos também podem levar água, sucos, chocolates e alimentos leves.

Não é permitido utilizar celulares, relógios de qualquer tipo ou outros equipamentos eletrônicos proibidos pelo edital.

Também são vedados corretivo líquido, lapiseira, caneta marca-texto, boné, chapéu e outros materiais que não sejam permitidos para a realização da prova.

Óculos inteligentes e armações com componentes eletrônicos integrados, como câmera, microfone, alto-falante, processador ou conectividade sem fio, também são proibidos.

Candidatos fazem prova do vestibular da Unicamp — Foto: Pedro Amatuzzi/g1

Os candidatos podem consultar o local de prova pela internet . A primeira fase será aplicada em 33 cidades no estado de São Paulo, além de seis capitais brasileiras. São elas:

Quando deve sair o resultado da primeira chamada?

A previsão para a divulgação da 1ª lista de aprovados é em 25 de janeiro de 2027, com a matrícula virtual agendada para ocorrer entre os dias 26 e 27.

Neste domingo (18), quem prestar a primeira fase do Vestibular 2027 da Unicamp poderá acompanhar a resolução comentada das questões, ao vivo, pelo g1 Campinas .

A transmissão começa às 15h, logo após o fim do exame , com professores analisando as perguntas e indicando as respostas corretas.

O programa será transmitido de um estúdio da EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, com a participação de jornalistas do portal e professores do colégio Oficina do Estudante.

logo que a prova acabar, os professores montarão uma força-tarefa para corrigir as 72 questões;

a cada resolução, os jornalistas farão contato com os professores, que entram ao vivo para comentar a questão e indicar a resposta;

em tempo real, os candidatos também poderão acessar o gabarito extraoficial, que será publicado no portal.

A cobertura começa antes mesmo de a prova terminar: equipes do g1 estarão nos locais de aplicação desde o início do dia, acompanhando a movimentação dos candidatos e trazendo as principais informações sobre o vestibular.

A transmissão faz parte do Vestibulou , projeto que reúne conteúdos para quem está se preparando para os vestibulares, com dicas de estudo, informações sobre as provas e reportagens especiais para ajudar na revisão dos conteúdos.

articles.summary: Apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado. Já os Bolões CAIXA nos canais eletrônicos ocorrem até as 10h45.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.071 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 170 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 11h deste domingo (11), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última quarta-feira (14), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Mexico arrests state official accused of allowing unauthorized CIA role in drug raid
articles.summary: Months after a deadly car wreck revealed the CIA’s participation in a raid on a Chihuahua drug lab, authorities arrested César Jáuregui, Chihuahua’s former attorney general, for allegedly allowing US spies to participate in the operation without permission from the Mexican government.
articles.body: Months after a deadly car wreck revealed the CIA’s participation in a raid on a Chihuahua drug lab, authorities arrested César Jáuregui, Chihuahua’s former attorney general, for allegedly allowing US spies to participate in the operation without permission from the Mexican government. Gilberto Loya Chávez, the acting head of the Chihuahua Attorney General’s Office, said in a video message that Jáuregui is under investigation for unlawful exercise of public service and conspiracy by public officials. Jáuregui is due to appear before a judge, Loya Chávez added, but did not say when. The arrest, the official explained, came after the Attorney General’s Office concluded that there had been misconduct in an April operation in which state officials dismantled a clandestine drug-manufacturing laboratory. The CIA’s participation came to light soon after the raid on April 19. That day, while he was still attorney general, Jáuregui himself announced that four people had died in a car crash as they were returning from a drug raid in northern Chihuahua: two Mexican law enforcement officials and two Americans, whom he identified as instructors from the US Embassy in Mexico City. Days later, CNN and other media outlets revealed that the two Americans were not just embassy workers: they were CIA agents. The agency has significantly expanded its clandestine anti-cartel operations in the country during President Donald Trump’s second term – including assassinations of alleged cartel members and drone flights over Mexican territory. On Saturday, Loya Chávez was careful to say that the issue at hand was not the drug raid itself, but rather the participation of US officials outside the bounds of Mexican law. “This action does not disregard the work of the State Investigation Agency, the State Attorney General’s Office, or the Armed Forces in dismantling the clandestine laboratory, because it is of course a very significant result in the fight against organized crime,” Loya Chávez said. “What is being investigated is the way this operation was conducted, the failure to observe the chain of command and the applicable protocols.” “A good result does not justify breaking the law,” the official added. CNN has contacted Jáuregui’s office to find out whether he already has legal representation and whether he has entered a plea. The presence of CIA agents in the operation incensed the government of President Claudia Sheinbaum, which took Chihuahua authorities to task for failing to give prior notice and coordinate with their federal counterparts, as required by Mexican law. Sheinbaum has insisted ever since that the situation had to be investigated to determine whether any crime had been committed. The president said at the time that her office had been unaware that state officials in Chihuahua and the US government were collaborating independently. “The relationship is federal, not state,” Sheinbaum said. “They must have authorization from the federal government for this collaboration, which necessarily takes place at the state level, as established by the Constitution.” Soon after, Chihuahua Governor María Eugenia Campos ordered the creation of a unit to investigate the case. On April 27, in her first report on the matter, special prosecutor Wendy Chávez said there were indications that the director of Chihuahua’s state security agency, who died in the car crash, had “possible unofficial collaboration” with the US agents and did not inform his superiors that they would be taking part in the operation. Jáuregui resigned as attorney general that same day, stating that he was accepting “political responsibility” for the tensions the matter had generated. “There were omissions both in the information provided and in the institutional handling of the points of contact with these individuals,” he said. Until his arrest on Saturday, Jáuregui had been seeking the conservative National Action Party nomination for mayor of Chihuahua, the state’s capital.

articles.title: Comedian Paul Whitehouse mugged at London cashpoint
articles.summary: His wife wrote on Instagram that the actor had been "mugged at a cash machine behind a Sainsbury's in Islington".
articles.body:
Actor and comedian Paul Whitehouse has fought back against someone who tried to steal his card at an London cash machine, according to his wife.

Dr Mine Conkbayir posted on Instagram that her husband had gone out to get some medication on Friday, when he was mugged at a cash machine behind a Sainsbury's in Islington.

"He did fight back and retrieved his card, with the perp scuttling away empty-handed," she wrote, warning people to be "super vigilant" out there.

The Welsh comedian, 68, is known for his work on The Fast Show and BBC's Gone Fishing.

In her post, Conkbayir said Whitehouse was picking up medication for her after she had a bad reaction to some treatment.

"Well, a horrid start to the weekend, would be an understatement," she wrote, adding that she had been encouraged by her husband to make the post "in the hope that it might help folk to be more aware when out and about".

Friends and fans alike have flooded to the comments of Conkbayir's post, condemning the attack and wishing Whitehouse a speedy recovery.

Among them were fellow comedian Dawn French, who wrote that the incident in Islington was "utterly not okay", and Angela Barnes, who said it was a "horrible thing to happen" and she was "sending love to you both".

Whitehouse is best known for his work on Gone Fishing, which he presents alongside fellow comedian Bob Mortimer.

The BBC Two series began in 2018 and sees Whitehouse and Mortimer discuss life while fishing. It has been nominated six times for a Bafta TV award.

The comedian has also been cast as Hogwarts caretaker Argus Filch in HBO's upcoming Harry Potter television series.

articles.title: Boy and man killed, 10 injured after woman drives through youth soccer game in Wichita, Kansas
articles.summary: A 6-year-old boy and 35-year-old man were killed, and 10 others were injured, when a woman drove a truck through a youth soccer game at a city sports complex in Wichita, Kansas, Saturday afternoon, police said.
articles.body: A 6-year-old boy and 35-year-old man were killed, and 10 others were injured, when a woman drove a truck through a youth soccer game at a city sports complex in Wichita, Kansas, Saturday afternoon, police said. The 34-year-old driver, from Garden City, Kansas, was in custody, though it wasn’t immediately clear if the incident at the Stryker Sports Complex was intentional, police said. “She has been cooperative up to this point in the investigation,” Wichita Police Capt. Aaron Moses said at an evening news conference. Both of the dead were from the city of McPherson, Moses said, but were not related to one another. The injured include five children, ranging in age from 5 to 9 years old, as well as five men and women between 28 and 68 years old, he said. “Those injuries span from minor injuries, like bruises, to extremely severe injuries,” the captain said. “But at this point, we believe those to be non-life-threatening.” An additional patient, a 61-year-old woman, was hospitalized with “non-traumatic medical issues,” he said. People began calling 911 shortly before 3:30 p.m., Moses said, “reporting that a vehicle had driven through a soccer game at Stryker Soccer Complex.” First responders, including Kansas Highway Patrol officers, Sedgwick County sheriff’s deputies and police from nearby Bel Aire, found the boy and the man dead at the scene, he said. They also saw bystanders tending to the injured. “They saw community members and citizens rendering medical aid to those who were injured,” he said. The driver was still in the truck, as were two children, Moses said. One of the women’s children had a game at the complex, though at a different field to where the crash occurred, he said. Wichita Mayor Lily Wu said on her personal Facebook page that the incident left her filled with sorrow. “I’m heartbroken by reports of a tragic incident at Stryker Sports Complex,” she said. “My thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected, especially the children and families involved.” Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly said in a statement that she’s monitoring the situation and has offered state resources to Wu. “My condolences go out to the families of the victims, the survivors, and all those impacted by this event,” she said, adding that she was “very grateful” to first responders. The Stryker Sports Complex is a city facility with 11 turf fields used for “all sports,” it states on its website. The city of Wichita said all events at the facility have been canceled for now. The Kansas State High School Activities Association said its scheduled flag football state championship has been suspended, along with any other of its matches through the weekend. An investigation into the incident was ongoing, police said. In a statement posted to Facebook, the Wichita Police Department asked anyone with video of the incident to upload it so investigators could take a look.

articles.title: New protein ranking names unexpected winner over beef, salmon and eggs
articles.summary: Tofu earned the top spot among 20 protein sources in a new BPI Score analysis, beating out beef, salmon, eggs and other animal-based options.
articles.body: A new analysis of 20 protein sources found that the top scorer wasn’t steak, salmon or eggs — it was an everyday food many shoppers may be overlooking. The BPI Score, introduced in a July paper published in the journal Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems, gave tofu the top mark: 36 out of 40 points. Beans, chia seeds and quinoa rounded out the top four, while mozzarella, lamb, beef and cheddar were among the lowest-ranked foods. The BPI Score, created by University of Cambridge researcher Chris Macdonald and the Better Protein Institute (BPI), rates 20 protein sources on a 40-point scale that combines nutrition, affordability and availability with environmental impact. AMERICANS STILL CRAVE PROTEIN DESPITE RECORD BEEF PRICES AS EXPERT REVEALS THE 'HEALTHIEST BURGER' Its "People Score" factors in sodium, saturated fat, cholesterol, whether a food contains all nine essential amino acids, affordability and availability. Its "Planet Score" considers greenhouse gas emissions, water pollution, land use and freshwater use. Tofu earned the highest scores in both categories. The paper estimated that producing 100 grams of protein from tofu was associated with 0.61 kilograms of greenhouse gas emissions, compared with 64.19 kilograms for beef. It also found tofu required about 2 square meters of land for that amount of protein, compared with about 211 square meters for beef. IS FARM-RAISED FISH REALLY WORSE THAN WILD-CAUGHT SEAFOOD? EXPERTS SOUND OFF Experts note that the ranking is an initial scoring system developed by one researcher, not a controlled trial or dietary guideline, and it relies on U.K. grocery data. The score also compares the amount of each food needed to provide 100 grams of protein, not equal-sized portions. "While acknowledging the limitations of this first iteration, the score provides a robust foundation for a more nuanced conversation," Macdonald wrote in the paper. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Corry Matthews, a California-based fitness and nutrition expert and founder of Strength & Grace Fitness, said consumers should consider protein quality, serving size and whether they can realistically get enough of a food to meet their needs. "For example, three ounces of cooked chicken breast provides roughly 26 grams of protein," Matthews told Fox News Digital. "A half cup of firm tofu may provide around 10 to 15 grams, depending on the product. Two tablespoons of chia seeds provide only about 4 to 5 grams." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER She continued, "That doesn't make chia seeds a bad food ... but I wouldn't rely on them as my primary protein source if my goal were to get 25 to 30 grams of protein at a meal." Animal proteins such as eggs, dairy, fish, and lean meats generally provide complete protein and can be concentrated sources of essential amino acids, she noted. Tofu, a soy food, is also a complete protein but those relying plant-based proteins may need to be more intentional about serving sizes and total intake, Matthews said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Ashley Koff, an Oregon-based registered dietitian and founder of The Better Nutrition Program, also said individual needs matter. "Many people do not digest tofu well at all," Koff said, adding that people should choose protein sources they enjoy and can access. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "My advice? Don't let a ranking do all your nutritional thinking for you," Matthews added. "Understand what the ranking measures, then choose foods that support your actual goals."

articles.body: BEND, Ore. — The Oregon school district that lost three young students and a teacher in a mass shooting this week expressed profound grief on Saturday, praising the courage of the educator and staff member who risked their lives during the attack. HERO DAD WHO TOOK DOWN OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER IDENTIFIED ALONG WITH TEACHER, STUDENT BOTH KILLED IN ATTACK The district remembered her as a bright light for her "students, family, and our community," adding, "She will be missed beyond words can express." "We continue to wrap our arms around Becky Drury," the post stated. "In addition, a learning specialist responded with extraordinary courage and engaged directly with the shooter. We are so thankful for her safety and forever in her debt." HERO DAD WHO TOOK DOWN OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER IDENTIFIED ALONG WITH TEACHER, STUDENT BOTH KILLED IN ATTACK The tragic shooting has devastated the community of Bend, located about 170 miles south of Portland. On Saturday, residents gathered near the school to mourn Lambert and the three young victims: 5-year-old Rhoam Summer, along with two other children, ages 8 and 11, whose families requested their names not be publicly disclosed. A 7-year-old girl and Drury both sustained injuries and are recovering, according to police. Giamanco was on his lunch break when he saw the teenage gunman entering the building with a shotgun. He retrieved a legally secured .40-caliber pistol from his car, pursued the shooter into the school, and fatally shot him. articles.title: Roman fort discovered in Pembrokeshire, Wales suggests the medieval legend of Emperor Magnus Maximus and his army camp may be true
articles.summary: For nearly seventeen centuries, a Welsh legend has claimed that a Roman emperor camped beside a hill in Pembrokeshire.
articles.body: For nearly seventeen centuries, a Welsh legend has claimed that a Roman emperor camped beside a hill in Pembrokeshire. Historians could never confirm it, because no Roman military site had been found near the spot. That has now changed. Archaeologists have uncovered a heavily fortified Roman fort in the Preseli Hills, together with fourth-century coins, tiles, pottery and the remains of a headquarters building. The discovery suggests the medieval tale of Macsen Wledig may rest on real history. Here is who found the fort, what the legend says, what the dig revealed, and why it matters for understanding Roman Wales.How archaeologist Mark Merrony found a hidden Roman fort near Frenni Fawr hill using satellite imageryThe fort was found by Mark Merrony, a leading Roman specialist at the University of Oxford, according to The Guardian. Merrony discovered it in 2024, about two miles, or three and a half kilometres, south-west of the summit of Frenni Fawr hill. Satellite imagery showed a convincing outline in an overgrown field. Shortly after he visited, a Roman tile caught his eye, the first of many. Merrony told The Guardian that the area is remote, yet the legend names the easternmost peak of the Preseli Hills, which is where the site lies. He was excited that this landscape holds the only Roman military site close to where the Mabinogion places the emperor, and "If Magnus Maximus was there, there must have been an army there."What the medieval Welsh tale of Macsen Wledig says about the Roman emperor Magnus Maximus and his campThe tale appears in the Mabinogion, a collection of medieval Welsh stories that blend legend, sorcery and marvels, which Merrony described to The Guardian as the Welsh counterpart of the Odyssey. In The Dream of Macsen Wledig, medieval storytellers used the emperor's name in Welsh to recount his rise to power. They described how, during his military manoeuvres, he pitched his camp at Frenni Fawr, which stands 395 metres, about 1,300 feet, high. Magnus Maximus governed Britain in the fourth century and campaigned against the Picts and the Scots, yet the idea that he also set up a camp in Wales had rested on folklore. Merrony told The Guardian that the legend has endured for nearly seventeen centuries.Why the headquarters building, commander's house and 500-soldier size point to a Roman military fortThe fort measures 180 by 150 metres, sits on a slope with a commanding view, and was probably home to about 500 troops. Merrony told The Guardian that it resembles a playing card, with rounded corners, and has a perpendicular road. A geophysical survey, which maps buried remains without digging, confirmed a rectangular building in the middle of the enclosure and a larger rectangular building immediately to its south. Merrony said this arrangement fits a headquarters building facing east toward the enemy and a commander's house. Extensive compacted clay floors, a common feature of Roman military sites, were also uncovered, and even rut marks left by wagons have been preserved. Together, these features support Merrony's conclusion that this was a genuine Roman military fort.Which finds from the dig, including two late fourth-century coins, link the site to the legendMerrony, while going over the time before the dig began, said his brother Nick jokingly asked him to find a couple of coins that would prove the Magnus Maximus theory. Nick then returned with two coins from the late fourth century and asked whether they were any good, which left Merrony astonished. Merrony told The Guardian it is fascinating to consider that the coins may be linked to the tale of Macsen Wledig. Other finds so far include an unusual iron stylus, many pottery shards and large quantities of Roman tiles. The excavation, funded by Oxford University and crowdfunding, was one of several planned and has just finished.Why the Pembrokeshire discovery challenges assumptions about Roman Wales and what the research will addMerrony also said that the presence of a heavily fortified Roman auxiliary fort may help unlock the mystery of the legend. The Guardian reports that the discovery overturns assumptions that the area's Indigenous Celtic tribe lived peacefully alongside the Roman invaders. It also builds on Merrony's earlier work, which includes two Roman villas, at Ford in Pembrokeshire and at Cutteslowe in Oxfordshire, and a Roman road along the southern shoulder of the Preseli Hills identified in 2022, which challenged the idea that the Romans did not venture far into Wales. His research will appear in Antiqvvs, a quarterly magazine about archaeology, ancient art and history, and Magnus Maximus will feature in his book Lives of the Roman Emperors, which Taylor and Francis describes as presenting concise biographies of ninety-five rulers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fears grow in DRC as former President Joseph Kabila joins rebellion
articles.summary: Kabila’s move raises new questions about the war in eastern Congo and prospects for peace.
articles.body:
Goma, DR Congo – Hopes for peace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have suffered another setback after former President Joseph Kabila joined a new political-military coalition challenging President Felix Tshisekedi.

Announced in Goma on Monday evening, the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), or Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, is led by Kabila and replaces the existing alliance between the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and the March 23 Movement (M23). The new coalition brings together figures and forces associated with the two movements, accuses Tshisekedi of tyranny and calls for resistance by all means, including force.

Goma, the main city in eastern Congo’s North Kivu province, has been under M23-AFC control since January last year. Kabila’s move brings a former head of state directly into the leadership of the rebellion.

The conflict has displaced millions and drawn in neighbouring countries. Its roots stretch back decades, shaped by regional rivalries, unresolved security concerns and competition for territory and mineral resources. The aftermath of Rwanda’s 1994 genocide helped fuel wars across the region, while tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali continue to shape the fighting.

M23 says it took up arms because the Congolese government failed to honour earlier commitments. The Congolese government and international actors have accused Rwanda of supporting the group, an allegation Kigali denies, citing security threats from armed groups operating in eastern Congo.

Whether Kabila’s leadership will reshape the rebellion or further complicate efforts to end the war remains unclear. In Goma, residents fear the latest realignment will push peace further out of reach.

Why do residents fear the war is far from over?

For Basa Juhudi, Kabila’s decision has revived fears that the conflict will drag on.

“As a resident of Goma, I believed the war might end in the very near future, hoping that the Congolese government would liberate us. And we are greatly surprised that even our former president has joined the fray,” he told Al Jazeera.

Juhudi said Kabila’s political experience makes his involvement particularly troubling.

“The fact that Joseph Kabila has joined the rebellion, bearing in mind that he is our former president and knows this country inside out, means the war is far from over. I am not happy about this frightening situation.”

He also fears for the country’s democratic future, recalling the peaceful transfer of power in 2019, when Tshisekedi succeeded Kabila.

“Today, I am very afraid. I don’t know if I will be lucky enough to experience a proper democracy in the DRC. I was delighted by the country’s very first peaceful transfer of power,” Juhudi said.

How does Kabila’s past shape his return to the conflict?

Kabila came to power in 2001 following the assassination of his father, Laurent-Desire Kabila. He was elected president in 2006 and re-elected in 2011.

His second constitutional term was due to end in 2016, but elections were delayed. Critics accused him of seeking to remain in power beyond the constitutionally permitted two terms. Protests against the delays were met with deadly violence before a political compromise paved the way for elections in December 2018.

Tshisekedi was declared the winner and took office in January 2019, marking the DRC’s first peaceful transfer of presidential power through elections. Kabila defended the election delays, arguing that the Congolese people had ultimately resolved their problems through dialogue.

His alignment with the FRN marks a new phase in his confrontation with Tshisekedi. The coalition presents itself as a political alternative to the government while maintaining an armed challenge to its authority. Whether Kabila can translate his political experience and networks into wider support remains uncertain.

Can dialogue still avert a wider confrontation?

Kabila’s move has drawn criticism from within the Congolese political establishment.

Vital Kamerhe, a former speaker of the National Assembly and leader of the Union for the Congolese Nation (UNC), urged the movement to abandon armed struggle.

“You cannot erase your own record by accusing your successor,” Kamerhe declared in a speech on Wednesday.

“I call on the leaders of this movement to abandon their plans and prioritise the path of dialogue. Whatever our frustrations, our differences or our ambitions, nothing, absolutely nothing, can justify us taking up weapons against our own country, at the risk of sacrificing our own Congolese lives,” he said.

His appeal highlights the central challenge facing peace efforts: political grievances remain unresolved, while renewed fighting threatens a population already battered by conflict.

What does Kabila’s move mean for peace initiatives?

The United States and Qatar have pursued separate diplomatic initiatives aimed at ending the conflict.

In Doha, representatives of the Congolese government and AFC-M23 have discussed a ceasefire, the return of refugees, the release of detainees and measures to counter rhetoric that stigmatises ethnic minorities.

Washington has pursued an agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, including commitments relating to the neutralisation of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and the withdrawal of Rwandan troops from Congolese territory.

The initiatives address different but connected dimensions of the crisis. Kabila’s emergence as leader of the FRN raises questions about who will represent the armed opposition and whether existing commitments will be respected.

However, the new coalition has said it intends to honour commitments made during the Doha negotiations.

In a communique released on Wednesday, Freddy Kaniki, one of the FRN’s leaders, said the signing of the coalition’s memorandum of association and its official launch marked the dissolution of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), which the FRN succeeds by right.

The communique said the FRN would assume the AFC’s “rights, obligations and commitments, in particular those entered into as part of the Doha negotiations”.

The statement suggests that the coalition intends to maintain the commitments made by its predecessor. It remains to be seen, however, how this pledge will translate into progress towards a ceasefire and a lasting settlement.

For Josue Akuzwe Walayi, a Congolese human rights activist, the development threatens to undermine hopes raised by the negotiations.

“My greatest fear is for the future of the Doha and Washington peace initiatives; it is not just that they will be a diplomatic failure, but that they will become yet more agreements without any real peace for the Congolese people,” he tells Al Jazeera.

Walayi argues that agreements without effective accountability mechanisms risk becoming empty promises. Lasting peace, he says, requires parties to honour their commitments and violations to be documented, investigated and punished in accordance with the law.

“What would the Doha and Washington agreements be worth if, despite the negotiations, Congolese people continue to die, families remain forced into exile and communities live in fear? The danger would be to normalise the war whilst the people pay the price,” he warns.

Could Kabila’s return pose a broader challenge to Kinshasa?

Kabila’s return to the centre of the conflict comes amid his legal confrontation with the Congolese state. Last year, a Congolese military court sentenced him to death in his absence on charges, including treason and war crimes, linking him to the M23 rebellion. His relatives described the conviction as “unjust” and “politically motivated”.

Goma resident Willo Riziki says Kabila’s involvement should prompt the government to reassess the challenge it faces.

“The Congolese authorities must now take this war very seriously. If Kinshasa thought it was dealing with puppets, that is no longer the case. There are people all over the country who remain loyal to Kabila,” Riziki told Al Jazeera.

How far that loyalty extends, and whether it can translate into organised political or military support, remains uncertain.

There has been no official government reaction to the coalition’s announcement. Last week, after Kabila warned that the country was in peril and needed to be saved, government spokesman Patrick Muyaya said the former president had “nothing to offer but chaos”. In a post on X, Muyaya described Kabila as a “man of the past, nostalgic for anti-democratic methods”.

The confrontation between Kabila and Tshisekedi reflects a wider struggle over the country’s political future. But for civilians in the east, the immediate question is whether the latest realignment will bring more fighting and further delay a negotiated settlement.

“We don’t know if the war will end here,” said Juhudi.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Starlink restrictions affect Ukraine but not Europe, disputes Musk’s technical explanation
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Elon Musk-owned SpaceX’s satellite systems remain in place,
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Elon Musk-owned SpaceX’s satellite systems remain in place, contradicting earlier indications that the service had been fully restored.The restrictions are affecting the Ukrainian military’s ability to use drones to intercept Russian attacks and deliver supplies to troops on the front lines, Zelenskyy said.The development has raised questions in Kyiv about whether the restrictions stem from a technical issue or a political decision by the Trump administration or SpaceX.Ukrainian officials told Axios that they had received conflicting explanations from the US government and SpaceX executives, with each side appearing to attribute responsibility to the other.“SpaceX as a company tells us it is a technical problem. But our contacts in the company say it is coming from the White House. When we ask the White House, they say it is Elon,” a Ukrainian official told Axios.Zelenskyy questions technical explanationZelenskyy said Ukraine had tested the satellite systems on Friday using cars travelling at high speeds in European Union countries and inside Ukraine.According to Ukrainian officials, Starlink and Starshield previously functioned on drones travelling at speeds of up to 400 kmph. The systems are now reportedly restricted to speeds of around 161 kmph.During the tests, the satellite systems continued working when cars travelled at 180 kmph in European Union countries. However, the connection dropped when the vehicles crossed into Ukraine at the same speed, Zelenskyy said.“The conclusion is that the restrictions apply inside Ukraine but do not apply in European Union countries. In other words, this is a planned operation,” he said.The Ukrainian president also expressed scepticism about SpaceX’s explanation that the speed restrictions were caused by technical problems.Why Starlink restrictions matter for UkraineUkraine relies heavily on SpaceX’s Starlink satellite network for military communications, logistics and the operation of reconnaissance and defensive drones.The systems enable Ukrainian forces to gather intelligence, intercept incoming Russian drones and support troops deployed along the front lines. Reduced functionality could also hamper Ukraine’s ability to conduct long-range strikes against Russian targets.Ukraine uses two satellite systems for different purposes. Starlink, operated by SpaceX, supports communications and defensive military operations, while Starshield is controlled by the US government and is used for offensive military purposes.Ukrainian officials have said restrictions affected both systems.You use AI every day.
